SingleReader is a performance hint to the channel; this publisher has one reader loop, and with the hint off the channel still delivers the same events in the same order, so no assertion can tell the two apart.

SingleWriter is a performance hint that lets the channel skip a lock; it changes only how the channel guards concurrent writers internally, never which events are delivered or in what order, so a test cannot observe it.
The call is guarded by Count == 1, so the collection is never empty and First() and FirstOrDefault() return the same item.

The rethrow of a cancelled send is followed by the loop reading the queue again with the same cancelled token, which throws the same cancellation at once, so the loop ends cancelled with or without the rethrow.

The early return stops a second flush loop starting while one runs. Without it the extra loop only waits on a timer, finds the batch already taken, and ends; the pushes and the resting flag are the same, so no test can reach a difference.

The catch block of the one reader returns nothing, and Stryker keeps the method returning its default, which is the same nothing, so a payload that is not JSON reads as null either way and no assertion can tell the two apart.

Which of the two waits finishes first when a job ends at the very moment the lane is stopped is decided by thread timing, not by anything a test can set; either way the lane asks for no more work, so this guard only closes a race.
An empty search pattern lists every file, exactly as the star does, so the folder listing is the same and no test can tell the two apart.
A relative path is never empty (the root itself reads as "."), so Split always has a first part and First() and FirstOrDefault() return the same.
A library that is not in the list makes First() throw, and the handler already falls back to the library id when the lookup throws, so the name it uses is the id either way.

The catch block of the payload reader returns nothing, and Stryker keeps the method returning its default, which is the same nothing, so a payload that is not JSON reads as null either way and no assertion can tell the two apart.
